headline: Contracts grow. Budgets swell. Space gets serious.
deck: This week, military contracts and funding rounds highlight a robust defense focus in space.

stories.head: Viasat lands $307 million military communications deal
stories.body: Viasat has secured a $307 million contract with the Marine Corps for satellite communications, ensuring the military's connectivity during operations. This win underscores the increasing reliance on satellite networks for defense, as traditional communication methods face challenges. With the growing demand for secure communication, this contract is a significant boost to Viasat's portfolio.
stories.soWhat: If the Marines need reliable Wi-Fi, it’s clear that terrestrial options are running thin.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190 million for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly has successfully raised $190 million in a Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. This funding will enhance its capabilities in co-orbital security and space domain awareness, areas increasingly prioritized by the Department of Defense. With defense budgets tightening, this cash injection may be just what True Anomaly needs to secure government contracts.
stories.soWhat: In a world where space is the new frontier for conflict, cash flow is the only thing that seems to matter.

stories.head: ESA and JAXA finalize Apophis mission agreement
stories.body: The European Space Agency (ESA) and Japan's JAXA have finalized an agreement to study the asteroid Apophis during its 2029 flyby. This collaboration highlights a strategic partnership in planetary defense, allowing both agencies to pool resources and expertise. As asteroid threats become more pressing, such partnerships are essential for global space safety.
stories.soWhat: If we can’t dodge asteroids, at least we can do it together.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Anduril and L3Harris
watchlist.body: Their joint tactical SDA constellation bid could reshape military space operations.

watchlist.title: Watch for updates on the FY27 budget
watchlist.body: The added $1.4 billion for space resilience indicates a shift in government priorities.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant launch
watchlist.body: With its critical design review cleared, the pressure is on for Sierra Space to deliver.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension
watchlist.body: The $480 million extension signals continued confidence in Palantir’s defense capabilities.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
